content.text:
I read the ticket and checked every claim against `main`. 

## The ticket's diagnosis is accurate

All four claims verify:

- **Sync writes the body into the wrong key.** `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept` (`apps/roam/src/utils/conceptConversion.ts:84`) does `literalContent.template = templateToText(node.template)`. The contract, as Obsidian's sync (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/conceptConversion.ts:57`) and both shared converters implement it, is `template` = title, `template_content` = body. The readers agree: `templateImport.ts:53` and `importNodes.ts:1266` read `template_content`. So Roam's flattened template currently reaches no reader — it's not just an inconsistency, it's dead data.
- **Publish drops template entirely.** `nodeSchemaToCrossApp` (`roamToCrossAppConverters.ts:202`) returns `localId, label, authorId, createdAt, modifiedAt, format, slotDefinitions` — no `template`/`templateTitle`, though `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` would happily write both.
- **Sync writes `literal_content.label` (last slash part), publish writes none.** Confirmed at `conceptConversion.ts:87-88` vs. `crossAppConverters.ts:98-103`.
- **`format` and `author_local_id` are already fine in both paths**, as the Notes say. The `missingNodeSchemas` filter (`publishNodesToGroups.ts:333`) does hide the divergence rather than fix it.

## One thing blocks implementation

**`label` has nowhere to live in the cross-app contract.** `CrossAppNodeSchema.label` is already spent: `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` maps it to the concept's `name`, and Roam sync sets `name` to the *full* `node.text`. Sync's `literal_content.label` is a *different* value — the last slash-separated part. One field can't carry both, so "use the same `label` in both paths" isn't implementable as written. Three ways out, and the ticket picks none:

1. Derive it in the shared `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` (last part of `node.label`) — cheapest, but it changes what Obsidian publishes too, where `label` is currently the whole name. That's a behavior change outside the stated scope.
2. Add a field to `CrossAppNodeSchema` (e.g. `shortLabel`) — cleanest semantically, but a contract change that the cross-app doc and `dbToCrossAppConverters` have to follow.
3. Drop `literal_content.label` from the Roam sync side instead and let `name` be the single source — arguably right, since nothing in the Roam path reads it, but it contradicts "preserving current sync behavior."

I'd argue for (2) if Obsidian's full-name `label` is deliberate, and (1) if it isn't — worth one question to Michael before starting.

## Smaller gaps, not blockers

- **`template`(title) is unreachable from Roam.** `DiscourseNode` (`getDiscourseNodes.ts:21-42`) has `template?: InputTextNode[]` and no title field. So "a template title only when one exists" means *never* on the Roam side. Fine, but the parity tests should assert it's absent rather than chase it.
- **"Same serialization"** means exporting `templateToText` (currently a module-private helper in `conceptConversion.ts:74`) and calling it from `nodeSchemaToCrossApp`. Unstated but obvious.
- **The `author_id` Done-When criterion isn't unit-testable.** "With the creator's account present, sync populates `author_id` and a later sync preserves it" is DB upsert behavior, not converter behavior — it needs an integration test against a real database, which the rest of the ticket's "focused tests" framing doesn't anticipate.
- **Round-trip parity has a leak the ticket doesn't mention.** `dbNodeSchemaToCrossApp` (`dbToCrossAppConverters.ts:126`) sweeps unrecognized `literal_content` keys into `metadata`, and `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` ignores `metadata` on the way back. So any key not explicitly handled is silently dropped on a db→crossApp→db trip. Whatever you decide for `label`, it has to be an explicit field on both sides or it won't survive the "publish then sync" direction the Done When asks about.

**Verdict:** well-researched ticket, correct problem statement, scope sensibly bounded. Ready to implement except for the `label` question — that one changes the shape of the diff (shared contract change vs. local fix), so it's worth resolving first rather than assuming. Want me to draft that question as a Linear comment?

Ok. I want to explore a bit, I'm not sure we have two label values. Splitting the DiscourseNode.text at slashes in conceptConversion:87 might have been a mistake; the DiscourseNode.text never has slashes, so this operation is likely a no-op.

content.text:
You're right. Both places that build `DiscourseNode.text` already strip the page prefix:

- The legacy path, `refreshConfigTree`, uses `title.substring("discourse-graph/nodes/".length)`.
- The new settings store, `getAllDiscourseNodes` in `accessors.ts`, uses `title.replace(DISCOURSE_NODE_PAGE_PREFIX, "")`.

So `text` is just the user's name for the type, e.g. `Claim`.

The history suggests how the split got there. It came in with the first version of `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept` (12b219038, ENG-332), which used it to compute `name`. That looks like it was written on the assumption that `text` was the full `discourse-graph/nodes/Claim` title. Later edits moved `name` to `node.text` and kept the split only for `literal_content.label`.

It isn't quite a no-op, though. Nothing stops someone from creating a type called `Foo/Bar`: `createDiscourseNode` builds the title as `${DISCOURSE_NODE_PAGE_PREFIX}${label}`, and I found no slash check in settings. The prefix strip then gives `text = "Foo/Bar"`, and the split would cut that down to `Bar`. So the one case where the split does anything is a case where it's wrong.

**There is only one label value, and that removes the blocker I raised.** The fix gets simpler:

- Roam sync drops the split and writes `literal_content.label = node.text`.
- `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` adds `label: node.label` to `literalInfo`.

This lines up with Obsidian, whose sync already writes `label: name`. So option 1 from my last message no longer changes Obsidian's behavior; it brings the shared converter in line with what Obsidian already does. I haven't checked Obsidian's publish path. If it goes through the same shared converter, it gains the same `label` key.

**Two things the ticket would need to change:**

- "Preserving current sync behavior" for `label` should become "`label` equals the schema name." The Done When test for "a slash-separated schema name" then checks that the name is kept whole, not split.
- Any existing record for a slash-named type keeps its truncated `label` until its next sync rewrites it. That's probably rare, and backfill is already out of scope.

Should I draft that correction as a Linear comment? Your memory notes say shared descriptions shouldn't be edited directly, so I'd post a comment rather than change the description.

content.text:
I've gone through the remaining points. Three are settled by what the code does; one needs your decision.

## Settled by the code

**1. Template title: Roam never has one.** `createDiscourseNode` in `accessors.ts` accepts `template` as either a block tree or a markdown string. A string is only a convenience at creation: it's converted into blocks under the `Template` child, and `DiscourseNode.template` is always `InputTextNode[]`. So `nodeSchemaToCrossApp` never sets `templateTitle`. The tests should check that `literal_content.template` is absent after both sync and publish. That also confirms the old sync-written `template` key is gone.

**2. "Same rules for absent optional fields" comes down to empty templates.** Here the two settings sources disagree:
- The new settings store turns an empty template into `undefined`: `settings.template.length > 0 ? settings.template : undefined` in `accessors.ts`.
- The legacy `getDiscourseNodes` path returns `[]` from `getSubTree(...).children`.
- `templateToText` also drops `{{…}}` blocks, so a template made only of buttons or queries turns into `""`.

Today, sync writes `template: ""` in the legacy case. The rule should be: serialize with `templateToText` and omit `template_content` when the result is empty. That rule belongs in one shared helper that both paths call. It can sit in `conceptConversion.ts`, exported, and be called from `nodeSchemaToCrossApp`.

**3. The round-trip leak doesn't apply here.** `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp` has one caller, `discoverSharedRelations.ts`, which reads other spaces' schemas and never writes them back. Both "sync then publish" and "publish then sync" go from Roam state to the database, so `metadata` is never part of either path. Also, with `label` now equal to `name`, nothing is lost there anyway.

## Needs your decision: the `author_id` criterion

`author_id` is filled in inside the database, not in the converters. `_local_concept_to_db_concept` (`concept.sql`) looks up `PlatformAccount` by `author_local_id`. The upsert's `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` then sets `author_id = db_concept.author_id` unconditionally. So a later sync keeps `author_id` only if it sends `author_local_id` again and the account still resolves. If either fails, the existing value is overwritten with NULL. That makes the criterion worth guarding, but only a database test can check it. `addConcepts.feature` has no scenario that upserts the same concept twice or checks `author_id`.

I'd split it into two tests:
- **Unit:** both `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept` and `nodeSchemaToCrossApp` → `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept` emit `author_local_id` = the creator's uid. This is cheap and runs in `test:unit`.
- **Cucumber:** one new scenario in `addConcepts.feature`: create the account, upsert a schema, check `author_id`, upsert it again, check it's still set. This is the only test that checks what the criterion actually says. It means running the suite, and your notes say to ask before that because it wipes the database.

The alternative is to settle for the unit test and reword the criterion to match. That's easier, but it leaves the NULL overwrite untested.

Which do you want? Once you pick, the ticket is ready and I'll start on the unit-level work either way.
I say settle for the unit test, add a note about the limitation.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

Scope note on the `author_id` criterion: the regression coverage will be unit-level only.

The tests will check that both Roam paths send `author_local_id` set to the schema creator's uid: sync through `discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`, and publish through `nodeSchemaToCrossApp` and `crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept`.

Limitation: the database, not the converters, turns `author_local_id` into `author_id`. The upsert's `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE` then sets `author_id` unconditionally. So a later upsert that omits `author_local_id`, or whose account doesn't resolve, overwrites an existing `author_id` with NULL. Unit tests can't catch that. Covering it needs a scenario in `addConcepts.feature` that upserts the same schema twice and checks `author_id` both times. This ticket doesn't add one.

content.text:
ENG-2202 is implemented in the working tree on `main`. Nothing is committed or branched. Both unit suites pass (Roam 537 tests, `packages/database` 61), both packages typecheck, and the changed files pass prettier.

**What changed:**
- **Sync** (`discourseNodeSchemaToLocalConcept`): the slash split is gone, so `label` is now `node.text`. The template body is written to `template_content` instead of `template`.
- **Publish** (`nodeSchemaToCrossApp`): now passes the template body through. It never sets a template title, because Roam doesn't have one.
- **Shared converter** (`crossAppNodeSchemaToDbConcept`): now writes `literal_content.label` alongside `name`. Only Roam's publish calls it, so Obsidian is unaffected.
- **New `nodeTemplateContent.ts`**: holds `templateToText`, moved out of `conceptConversion.ts` unchanged, plus the rule for leaving the field out. An empty template, or one with only `{{…}}` components, gets no `template_content`. Both paths call it, so they can't drift apart.

**Tests:**
- **Parity** (new `schemaMetadataParity.test.ts`): runs six schemas through both paths and checks they send identical `name`, `source_local_id`, `author_local_id`, `literal_content` and `local_reference_content`. The six cover templates, source slots, both, neither, a template of only components, and a slash in the name. Timestamps and space fields aren't compared. To check the test can fail, I took the `label` line out of the shared converter: six of the seven failed. The line is restored.
- **Per-converter**: each path's own test file covers template, empty template and slash-in-name cases. The shared converter's tests now expect `label`.
- **`author_local_id`**: covered in both paths. The sync test has a comment saying the database-side overwrite isn't covered, matching your Linear note.

**Worth knowing:**
- A nested template serializes with a stray `"   \n"` line, because `indent` also pads the trailing newline. That's existing behavior, and I kept it so the stored value doesn't change. The test pins it as-is. Fixing it would change every nested template the next time it syncs.
- Existing schema rows keep their old `literal_content.template` key until the next sync rewrites them. No backfill, per the ticket.
- I haven't run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm ci:validate`. That's the step before calling this PR-ready, once you've put it on a branch.

I shortened two comments. The first is the one you likely meant:

- **The `author_id` note on the sync test** went from three lines to one: `// Not covered: an upsert whose author_local_id doesn't resolve nulls author_id.` It still names the gap your Linear note describes. The explanation of why lives in Linear.

I left the two comments in the parity test alone. Each is one line and explains something a reader would otherwise have to work out: why the fake Roam API answers both the sync and publish lookups, and why timestamps aren't compared. Prettier is clean, and the sync tests still pass.
